clue.text: Play area in revolutionary nursery

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary
short for recreation ground, a public playground

explanation.surface: A children's play corner inside a nursery with a radical streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play area' looks like part of the definition, but it is the inner piece; Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A crèche is a day nursery where young children are looked after while parents work or shop.

clue.text: Make reference to installing electrical units for outdoor holiday venue

indicators.note: to install something is to put it inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: to cite is to refer to or quote
amperes, units of electric current

explanation.surface: An instruction to mention the power points at a caravan park.
explanation.definitionFit: A campsite is a place for pitching tents on holiday in the open air.

clue.text: English partygoer getting in the groove?

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person doing it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a raver is someone at a rave, a wild party

explanation.surface: An English clubber is dancing in the groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the groove' suggests dancing to the beat; read literally, it is someone cutting grooves into metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver incises lines into a surface, so cryptically they are one who gets into grooves.

clue.text: Get about 50 to split equally

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: to get something is to come to have it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Collect around fifty in order to share them out evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to divide it into two equal parts.

clue.text: Official aid I once refused is reduced

indicators.note: refused one time means the letter is turned away on just one of its appearances

blocks.note: grants of public money
taken as written; the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A government grant is cut because someone turned it down at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: SUBSIDIES has two Is; 'once' says only one goes, leaving SUBSIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: When a storm or swelling subsides it diminishes, which is to say it is reduced in strength or size.

clue.text: Erratic jockey reclined at pub

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre and jostle, so the letters are pushed into new positions

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wayward jockey lounged in the pub instead of riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' looks like a person who reclined; it is a verb telling you to shuffle the letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is irregular and inconsistent, impossible to forecast.

clue.text: One suffering heat burns?

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked about and damaged, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who gets burnt by the sun's heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, and its last two words also supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbather lies in strong sunshine and risks sunburn, so is someone who may suffer burns from heat.

clue.text: Arguments between start and end of day dropping off

indicators.note: the start and end of a word are its outermost letters, so only those two are kept
a thing between two others is enclosed by them on either side

blocks.note: first and last letters
rows are quarrels

explanation.surface: Quarrelling from morning to night leaves one ready to nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a row (rhyming with cow) is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drowsy is sleepy, on the point of dropping off to sleep.

clue.text: Workers' group cutting drinks gradually as part of fitness regime

indicators.note: something cutting into another breaks into it, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: to sip is to drink a little at a time
trade union

explanation.surface: A union is reducing its members' drinking as part of a health drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are abdominal exercises, a staple element of a workout routine.

clue.text: Second heave turned round big gun

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the word for heave is read backwards

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo'
to lug is to haul or heave something heavy

explanation.surface: An artillery crew heaves a cannon round in a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A big gun is slang for an important, powerful person, and a mogul is a magnate of that kind.

clue.text: Killing Greek character housed in annexe abroad

indicators.note: a thing housed in a building is lodged within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a wing is an annexe added to a building
a letter of the Greek alphabet
out and about, away from home

explanation.surface: A Greek is murdered while staying in a building extension overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek letter sits after the first two letters of the annexe, not at its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiping out a population or army means destroying it entirely, a figurative and literal form of killing.

clue.text: Delay on radio before cancelling Olympic sport

indicators.note: words on the radio are only heard, so what counts is the sound

blocks.note: to wait is to delay
lifting a ban or restriction cancels it

explanation.surface: A broadcast is postponed ahead of an Olympic event being called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Weightlifting, raising heavy barbells, is one of the events contested at the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Do without porridge when we're not busy?

definitions.note: a phrase describing the noun phrase's time, not a noun itself; the question mark flags the looseness

blocks.note: to spare something is to manage without it
porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, which is 'doing time'

explanation.surface: Skipping the breakfast oats is something to do on a lazy day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' looks like breakfast; it is British slang for time served in jail, made famous by the sitcom of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare time is leisure, the hours free from work or obligations.

clue.text: Sit back beside Athens' foremost storyteller

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its very beginning, so only its opening letter is kept
sitting back here is read as the word for sit going backwards

blocks.note: first letter of the city name
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Relax beside the leading teller of tales in ancient Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of the famous animal fables, the classic storyteller.

clue.text: Play as reserve in Arthur's cricket team, we're told?

indicators.note: something we are told is heard rather than read, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: a cricket side has eleven players, with a twelfth man as reserve; King Arthur's men were knights

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a play as the substitute for King Arthur's cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the twelfth man is the substitute who stands by for the eleven; give Arthur a team of knights and the reserve is a twelfth knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelfth Night is Shakespeare's comedy, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: Obsessive thief's reformed first

indicators.note: something reformed is formed again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A compulsive thief's criminal reform comes before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetishist has a fixation on some object or practice, so is an obsessive.

clue.text: North American jail in which boy turns up or Russian girl goes down

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the boy's name runs backwards
the jail is something in which the other piece is placed

blocks.note: can is slang for prison
a boy's name

explanation.surface: A North American jailbird whose son is upside down or daughter is heading lower.
explanation.walkthrough: AIDAN reversed is NADIA, a Russian girl's name, so the clue offers both ways of reading the inner piece: the boy going up or the girl going down.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian is a native of Canada, a North American country.

clue.text: Intellectual brother tucking into cornflakes, perhaps

indicators.note: tucking into food literally means getting inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: cornflakes are an example of breakfast cereal
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A clever sibling digging into a bowl of breakfast flakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' sounds like eating; here it means going inside. 'Perhaps' marks cornflakes as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral means of the brain, so appealing to the intellect rather than the emotions.

clue.text: Real data Tate assembles in due course

indicators.note: to assemble is to put parts together in a new form, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The Tate gallery will compile its genuine figures eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean eventually, at some future time not yet fixed.

clue.text: Bridge supporters chief opponents in the game

blocks.note: arch- means chief, as in archbishop
in the card game bridge, East and South sit on opposing sides

explanation.surface: The main rivals in a bridge game have their backers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The game' points back to bridge the card game, whose four players are named by compass points; the definition means bridge as a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Arches are the curved structures holding up a bridge, so they support it.

clue.text: Beetle about to be spotted amidst railings, climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top
something spotted amidst others is seen in their midst, placed inside

blocks.note: bars making up a fence
abbreviation of circa, about

explanation.surface: An insect is about to be seen crawling up the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is placed after the first letter of the upturned SRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Torments leader going off the rails

indicators.note: when the leader goes off, the front letter departs and the rest remains

blocks.note: railway lines, as in going off the tracks

explanation.surface: A boss who is losing the plot makes the staff suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off the rails' reads as an idiom for misbehaving, but it splits: the leader of the rails goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rack someone is to torture them, from the medieval stretching device, so racks is a synonym for torments.

clue.text: Devise a building block, briefly dipping into fortune

indicators.note: kept brief means cut short, so the final letter is lopped off
dipping into something means going inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: fate is one's fortune or lot
taken as written
a brick is the basic building block

explanation.surface: Plan to make a toy brick while taking a chance on luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building block' looks like part of the definition; it is the piece cut short and slipped into fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate is to make up or construct something, which is to devise it.

clue.text: Son leaves only hint

indicators.note: when someone leaves they depart, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: abbreviation for son; the letter removed
simply means only, merely

explanation.surface: A son goes, giving no more than a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to suggest something indirectly, which is to hint at it.

clue.text: Police boarding car in film to find killer

indicators.note: people boarding a vehicle get inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Herbie is the Volkswagen Beetle in Disney's The Love Bug films
the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's detective branch

explanation.surface: Detectives search a movie car looking for a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of a British police force. Herbie is the Disney car with a mind of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbicide is a weedkiller, a chemical that destroys plants.

clue.text: Former deputy at Abbey

blocks.note: first meaning: earlier, previous
second meaning: the monk ranking just below the abbot

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an ex-deputy at a particular abbey; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier, and a prior is also the officer second in command of an abbey under the abbot.

clue.text: Boat smashed in judicious action by wrecker

indicators.note: something smashed is broken up into pieces that can be rearranged
one part placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
sage means wise and judicious

explanation.surface: A vessel is wrecked by a deliberate, calculated act of destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By wrecker' belongs to the definition: sabotage is the action a wrecker takes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate damage done to obstruct or destroy, the work of a wrecker.

clue.text: Songbook from Milan my husband sent back

indicators.note: letters taken from a word are lifted out of it, here its tail end
things sent back travel the other way, so the string is read in reverse

blocks.note: the closing letters of the city name
taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife's husband returns a hymn book bought in Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns, a collection of songs for worship.
